questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following curve represents the first order reaction ?
questions.solution: For a first order reaction, half-life is independent of initial reactant concentration: $t_{1/2} = \frac{0.693}{k}$. Therefore, a plot of $t_{1/2}$ versus $[R]_0$ is a horizontal straight line parallel to the concentration axis, as shown in curve (B).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following solutions will have the lowest freezing point in water ?
questions.solution: Depression in freezing point $\Delta T_f = i \cdot K_f \cdot m$. $\text{CaCl}_2$ dissociates into 3 ions ($i = 3$), giving the highest van 't Hoff factor and hence maximum freezing point depression, resulting in the lowest freezing point.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following is not a transition metal ?
questions.solution: Mercury (Hg) has completely filled d-orbitals ($5d^{10}$) in its ground state as well as in its common oxidation states, so it is not considered a transition element.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following represents the fraction of molecules with energies equal to or greater than $E_a$ ?
questions.solution: According to the Boltzmann distribution / Arrhenius equation, the fraction of molecules having kinetic energy equal to or greater than activation energy $E_a$ is given by $x = e^{-E_a/RT}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: What will happen during the electrolysis of aqueous solution of $\text{CuCl}_2$ by using platinum electrodes ?
options: (B) $\text{H}_2$ gas will be released at cathode
(C) $\text{O}_2$ gas will be released at anode
(D) $\text{Cl}_2$ gas will be released at anode
questions.solution: During electrolysis of aqueous $\text{CuCl}_2$, $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ ions are reduced to Cu metal at the cathode due to higher reduction potential than $\text{H}^+$. At the anode, $\text{Cl}^-$ is oxidized to $\text{Cl}_2$ gas in preference to water oxidation due to the overpotential of oxygen gas generation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Aspirin is obtained by acetylation of
questions.solution: Acetylation of 2-hydroxybenzoic acid (salicylic acid) with acetic anhydride in the presence of an acid catalyst produces acetylsalicylic acid (aspirin).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The secondary valency of Co in the complex $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5(\text{NO}_2)]^{2+}$ is
questions.solution: Secondary valency corresponds to the coordination number of the central metal ion. Here, five $\text{NH}_3$ ligands and one $\text{NO}_2^-$ ligand coordinate to Co, giving a coordination number of 6.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: At low temperature, phenol reacts with dil. $\text{HNO}_3$ to yield
questions.solution: Phenol reacts with dilute nitric acid at low temperature (298 K) to give a mixture of ortho-nitrophenol and para-nitrophenol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following is 'not' true about enantiomers ?
options: (A) They have the same chemical reactivity.
(B) They have the same specific rotation.
(C) They have the same melting or boiling point.
(D) They have the same refractive index.
questions.solution: Enantiomers have specific rotations equal in magnitude but opposite in sign (+ and -). Thus, saying they have the 'same specific rotation' without specifying magnitude/sign is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Aniline on direct nitration yields
questions.solution: Direct nitration of aniline in strongly acidic medium leads to protonation of aniline forming anilinium ion (meta-directing). Hence, a significant amount of meta-derivative is formed along with ortho and para products: 51% para, 47% meta, and 2% ortho derivatives.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following amines has lowest $pK_b$ value ?
questions.solution: Lowest $pK_b$ value corresponds to the strongest base. $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{N}(\text{CH}_3)_2$ has two electron-releasing methyl groups ($+I$ effect) attached to the nitrogen atom, increasing the electron density on nitrogen compared to aniline and monomethylaniline.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The deficiency of which of the following vitamins causes increased fragility of red blood cells and muscular weakness :
questions.solution: Deficiency of Vitamin E causes increased fragility of RBCs and muscular weakness.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Assertion (A) : It is not possible to separate the components of an azeotrope by fractional distillation.
Reason (R) : Components of an azeotrope have the same composition in liquid and vapour phase and boil at a constant temperature.
options: (A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
(B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
(C) Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
(D) Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: Azeotropes boil at a constant temperature and have identical composition in both liquid and vapour phases. Therefore, their components cannot be separated by fractional distillation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Assertion (A) : The presence of $-\text{OH}$ group in phenols directs the incoming group to meta position in the ring.
Reason (R) : $-\text{OH}$ group in phenols activates the aromatic ring towards electrophilic substitution reaction.
options: (A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
(B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
(C) Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
(D) Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: The $-\text{OH}$ group in phenols is ortho- and para-directing, not meta-directing due to $+M$ resonance effect. Thus, Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Assertion (A) : Actinoids show wide range of oxidation states.
Reason (R) : Actinoids are radioactive in nature.
options: (A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
(B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
(C) Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
(D) Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: Actinoids show a wide range of oxidation states because the $5f, 6d$ and $7s$ energy levels are of comparable energies. It is also true that actinoids are radioactive, but radioactivity is not the reason for their variable oxidation states.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Assertion (A) : The pentaacetate of glucose does not react with $\text{H}_2\text{N}-\text{OH}$.
Reason (R) : It indicates the presence of free $-\text{CHO}$ group in glucose.
options: (A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
(B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
(C) Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
(D) Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: Glucose pentaacetate does not react with hydroxylamine because the cyclic hemiacetal form is locked, indicating the absence (not presence) of a free $-\text{CHO}$ group. Thus, Assertion is true but Reason is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
What type of deviation from Raoult's law is shown by a mixture of phenol and aniline ? Give reason.
What will happen to the boiling point of the solution on mixing phenol and aniline ?
questions.solution:
1. Phenol and aniline mixture shows negative deviation from Raoult's law.
2. Reason: Phenolic proton forms strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding with the lone pair on nitrogen of aniline. The intermolecular attractive forces between phenol and aniline ($A-B$) are stronger than $A-A$ and $B-B$ interactions.
3. Due to negative deviation, the vapour pressure decreases, so the boiling point of the solution increases.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Why are haloarenes less reactive towards nucleophilic substitution reaction ? Give two reasons.
questions.solution:
Haloarenes are less reactive towards nucleophilic substitution reactions due to:
1. Resonance effect: The lone pairs on halogen atom delocalize with the $\pi$-electrons of the benzene ring, imparting partial double bond character to the C-X bond, making it difficult to break.
2. $sp^2$ Hybridization of carbon: The carbon attached to halogen is $sp^2$ hybridized, which is more electronegative and holds the C-X bond tightly compared to $sp^3$ carbon in haloalkanes.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
(a) Write IUPAC names of the following coordination compounds :
(i) $[\text{Ag}(\text{NH}_3)_2] [\text{Ag}(\text{CN})_2]$
(ii) $\text{K}_3[\text{Fe}(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4)_3]$

OR

(b) (i) Give a chemical test to show that $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{SO}_4]\text{Cl}$ and $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]\text{SO}_4$ are ionisation isomers.
(ii) What is meant by the 'Chelate effect' ? Give an example.
questions.solution:
(a) (i) Diammineargentum(I) dicyanidoargentate(I)
(ii) Potassium trioxalatoferrate(III)

OR

(b) (i) Add $\text{AgNO}_3$ solution: $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{SO}_4]\text{Cl}$ gives a white precipitate of $\text{AgCl}$, whereas $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]\text{SO}_4$ gives no reaction. Alternatively, add $\text{BaCl}_2$ solution: $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]\text{SO}_4$ gives a white precipitate of $\text{BaSO}_4$.
(ii) Chelate effect: The extra stability acquired by a complex compound when multidentate ligands bind to a central metal ion to form stable ring structures is called the chelate effect. Example: $[\text{Co}(\text{en})_3]^{3+}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Differentiate between the following :
(i) Peptide linkage and Glycosidic linkage
(ii) Essential amino acids and Non-essential amino acids
questions.solution:
(i) Peptide linkage is an amide bond ($-\text{CO}-\text{NH}-$) formed between $-\text{COOH}$ and $-\text{NH}_2$ groups of two amino acid molecules in proteins. Glycosidic linkage is an ether linkage ($-\text{C}-\text{O}-\text{C}-$) formed between two monosaccharide units through an oxygen atom in carbohydrates.
(ii) Essential amino acids cannot be synthesized by the human body and must be supplied through diet (e.g., Valine, Leucine). Non-essential amino acids can be synthesized in the body (e.g., Glycine, Alanine).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Following reaction takes place in one step :
$$2\text{A} + \text{B} \longrightarrow 2\text{C}$$
How will the rate of above reaction change if the volume of the reaction vessel is decreased to one third of its original volume ? Will there be any change in the order of reaction with the reduced volume ?
questions.solution:
Since the reaction takes place in one step (elementary reaction):
Rate law: $r_1 = k [\text{A}]^2 [\text{B}]$
When volume is reduced to $V/3$, concentrations become 3 times:
$[\text{A}'] = 3[\text{A}]$ and $[\text{B}'] = 3[\text{B}]$
New rate: $r_2 = k (3[\text{A}])^2 (3[\text{B}]) = 27 k [\text{A}]^2 [\text{B}] = 27 r_1$
So the rate increases by 27 times.
There will be NO change in the order of reaction (it remains 3rd order overall).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
For the first order thermal decomposition reaction, following data was obtained :
$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl}(g) \longrightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_4(g) + \text{HCl}(g)$$

| S. No. | Time (s) | Total Pressure (atm) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0 | 0.30 |
| 2 | 30 | 0.50 |

Calculate rate constant. [Given : $\log 3 = 0.48$]
questions.solution:
Let initial pressure $P_i = 0.30\text{ atm}$.
At time $t = 30\text{ s}$, let decrease in pressure of reactant be $x$.
$\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl}(g) \longrightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_4(g) + \text{HCl}(g)$
At $t=0$: $P_i$, $0$, $0$
At $t=30$: $P_i - x$, $x$, $x$
Total pressure $P_t = P_i + x = 0.50\text{ atm} \implies x = 0.50 - 0.30 = 0.20\text{ atm}$.
Pressure of $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl}$ at $t=30\text{ s}$ is $P_A = P_i - x = 0.30 - 0.20 = 0.10\text{ atm}$.
Rate constant $k = \frac{2.303}{t} \log \frac{P_i}{P_A} = \frac{2.303}{30} \log \frac{0.30}{0.10} = \frac{2.303}{30} \log 3$
$k = \frac{2.303 \times 0.48}{30} = \frac{1.10544}{30} = 0.0368\text{ s}^{-1} = 3.68 \times 10^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
(a) Answer the following :
(i) Why is the Equilibrium Constant ($K_c$) related to $E^\circ_{\text{cell}}$ and not to $E_{\text{cell}}$ ?
(ii) Two metals 'A' and 'B' have standard electrode potential values of $-0.24\text{ V}$ and $+0.80\text{ V}$ respectively. Which of these will liberate hydrogen gas from dil. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ ?
(iii) Write the cell reaction which occurs in lead storage battery when it is in charging.

OR

(b) What type of battery is Mercury cell ? Why it is more advantageous than dry cell ? Write overall reaction taking place in Mercury cell.
questions.solution:
(a) (i) At equilibrium, $E_{\text{cell}} = 0$, whereas $E^\circ_{\text{cell}}$ is a constant at a given temperature and directly related to $K_c$ by $\Delta G^\circ = -nFE^\circ_{\text{cell}} = -RT \ln K_c$.
(ii) Metal 'A' ($-0.24\text{ V}$) will liberate $\text{H}_2$ gas because its standard reduction potential is lower (more negative) than $\text{H}^+/\text{H}_2$ ($0.00\text{ V}$).
(iii) Charging reaction of lead storage battery:
$$2\text{PbSO}_4(s) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l) \longrightarrow \text{Pb}(s) + \text{PbO}_2(s) + 2\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4(aq)$$

OR

(b) Mercury cell is a primary battery. It is advantageous because its cell potential remains constant ($1.35\text{ V}$) during its lifetime as no ion in solution is consumed/produced whose concentration changes. Overall reaction:
$$\text{Zn(Hg)} + \text{HgO}(s) \longrightarrow \text{ZnO}(s) + \text{Hg}(l)$$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Calculate the boiling point of a solution containing $0.61\text{ g}$ of benzoic acid (Molar mass $= 122\text{ g mol}^{-1}$) in $5\text{ g}$ of $\text{CS}_2$ in which it dimerises to the extent of $88\%$. The boiling point and $K_b$ of $\text{CS}_2$ are $46.2^\circ\text{C}$ and $2.3\text{ K kg mol}^{-1}$ respectively.
questions.solution:
1. Dimerization: $2 \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COOH} \rightleftharpoons (\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COOH})_2$
Degree of association $\alpha = 0.88$, $n = 2$.
van 't Hoff factor $i = 1 - \alpha\left(1 - \frac{1}{n}\right) = 1 - 0.88(1 - 0.5) = 1 - 0.44 = 0.56$.
2. Molality $m = \frac{w_b / M_b}{W_a \text{ (in kg)}} = \frac{0.61 / 122}{5 / 1000} = \frac{0.005}{0.005} = 1.0\text{ m}$.
3. Elevation in boiling point $\Delta T_b = i \cdot K_b \cdot m = 0.56 \times 2.3 \times 1.0 = 1.288^\circ\text{C}$.
4. Boiling point of solution $T_b = T_b^\circ + \Delta T_b = 46.2 + 1.288 = 47.488^\circ\text{C}$ (or $47.49^\circ\text{C}$).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Write the reactions of D-Glucose with the following :
(a) HI
(b) $\text{Br}_2$ water
(c) Conc. $\text{HNO}_3$
questions.solution:
(a) Prolonged heating with HI reduces glucose to n-hexane:
$$\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6 \xrightarrow{\text{HI, } \Delta} \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$$
(b) Reaction with mild oxidizing agent $\text{Br}_2$ water oxidizes $-\text{CHO}$ to $-\text{COOH}$, forming Gluconic acid:
$$\text{CHO}-(\text{CHOH})_4-\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \xrightarrow{\text{Br}_2/\text{H}_2\text{O}} \text{COOH}-(\text{CHOH})_4-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$
(c) Conc. $\text{HNO}_3$ oxidizes both aldehyde and primary alcohol groups to dicarboxylic acid, forming Saccharic acid (Glucaric acid):
$$\text{CHO}-(\text{CHOH})_4-\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \xrightarrow{\text{Conc. HNO}_3} \text{COOH}-(\text{CHOH})_4-\text{COOH}$$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Give reasons for the following :
(a) Carboxylic acids have higher boiling point than alcohols of comparable molecular masses.
(b) Alpha ($\alpha$) hydrogens of aldehydes and ketones are acidic in nature.
(c) Nucleophilic addition of ammonia and its derivatives does not occur with carbonyl group in strongly acidic medium.
questions.solution:
(a) Carboxylic acid molecules form stronger extensive intermolecular hydrogen bonds and exist as stable dimers even in the vapour phase, leading to higher boiling points than alcohols.
(b) The $\alpha$-hydrogens are acidic because loss of $\text{H}^+$ yields a conjugate base (enolate ion) which is stabilized by resonance with the adjacent electron-withdrawing carbonyl group.
(c) In strongly acidic medium, ammonia and its derivatives get protonated to form non-nucleophilic ammonium salts (e.g., $\text{R-NH}_3^+$), leaving no lone pair available to attack the carbonyl carbon.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Write the reaction involved in the following :
(a) Reimer-Tiemann reaction
(b) Kolbe's reaction
(c) Friedel-Crafts acylation of anisole
questions.solution:
(a) Reimer-Tiemann reaction:
$$\text{Phenol} + \text{CHCl}_3 + 3\text{NaOH} \xrightarrow{340\text{ K}} \text{Salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde)} + 3\text{NaCl} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
(b) Kolbe's reaction:
$$\text{Phenol} \xrightarrow{\text{NaOH}} \text{Sodium phenoxide} \xrightarrow[\text{H}^+]{\text{CO}_2, 400\text{ K, 4-7 atm}} \text{2-hydroxybenzoic acid (Salicylic acid)}$$
(c) Friedel-Crafts acylation of anisole:
$$\text{Anisole} + \text{CH}_3\text{COCl} \xrightarrow{\text{Anhyd. AlCl}_3} 2-\text{methoxyacetophenone} + 4-\text{methoxyacetophenone (major)}$$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Compound 'X' with molecular formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_9\text{Br}$ reacts with aqueous KOH to give an alcohol. The rate of this reaction depends only on the concentration of the compound 'X'. When an optically active isomer 'Y' of the compound 'X' was treated with aqueous KOH solution, the rate of reaction was found to be dependent on concentration of compound 'Y' and aqueous KOH both.
(a) Write down the structural formula of both 'X' and 'Y'.
(b) Out of 'X' and 'Y', which one will undergo racemisation and why ?
(c) Out of 'X' and 'Y', which one will form product with inversion of configuration and why ?
questions.solution:
(a) 'X' undergoes $S_N1$ mechanism (rate depends only on [X]): 2-Bromo-2-methylpropane, $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-Br}$.
'Y' is an optically active isomer undergoing $S_N2$ mechanism: 2-Bromobutane, $\text{CH}_3\text{-CH(Br)-CH}_2\text{-CH}_3$.
(b) 'X' will undergo racemisation because it proceeds via planar carbocation intermediate ($S_N1$), allowing attack from either face equally.
(c) 'Y' will form product with inversion of configuration because it proceeds via $S_N2$ mechanism involving backside attack of the nucleophile.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Case-based questions on Amines:
(a) (i) Why $\text{CH}_3-\text{NH}_2$ is a stronger base than $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{N}$ in aqueous solution ?
(ii) Write structural formulae of the compound A and B :
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CONH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{NaOBr}} A \xrightarrow[\text{Base}]{\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCl}} B$$

(b) A compound 'X' with molecular formula $\text{C}_3\text{H}_9\text{N}$ reacts with Hinsberg reagent to give a product insoluble in alkali. Identify 'X'.
OR
(b) How can you convert aniline to benzonitrile ?

(c) Why is $-\text{NH}_2$ group of aniline acetylated before carrying out nitration ?
questions.solution:
(a) (i) In aqueous solution, the substituted ammonium cation of primary amine $\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_3^+$ is extensively stabilized by hydrogen bonding (solvation) compared to the cation of tertiary amine $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{NH}^+$ which has steric hindrance.
(ii) $A = \text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2$ (Methanamine via Hofmann bromamide degradation).
$B = \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CONHCH}_3$ (N-methylbenzamide).

(b) Compound 'X' reacts with Hinsberg reagent to give alkali-insoluble product, indicating it is a secondary amine: N-methylethanamine / Dimethylamine, $\text{CH}_3\text{-NH-C}_2\text{H}_5$.
OR
(b) Convert Aniline to Benzonitrile:
1. Aniline $\xrightarrow{\text{NaNO}_2 + \text{HCl, 273-278 K}} \text{Benzene diazonium chloride} (\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{N}_2^+\text{Cl}^-)$.
2. $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{N}_2^+\text{Cl}^- \xrightarrow{\text{CuCN/KCN}} \text{Benzonitrile} (\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CN})$.

(c) $-\text{NH}_2$ group is acetylated to protect it and decrease its activating power (resonance with acetyl carbonyl group), preventing ring over-activation and oxidative destruction by nitric acid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Case-based questions on Coordination Compounds:
(a) In octahedral crystal field, energies of which d-orbitals will be raised when ligands approach the central metal atom/ion ? Give reason in support of your answer.
(b) Using crystal field theory, write the electronic configuration of central metal atom/ion of the following :
(i) $[\text{CoF}_6]^{3-}$
(ii) $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$  [At. No. : Co = 27]
(c) $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$ is paramagnetic while $[\text{Ni(CO)}_4]$ is diamagnetic though both are tetrahedral. Why ? [Atomic No. : Ni = 28]
OR
(c) Write hybridization and magnetic behaviour of the complex $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{3-}$. [Atomic No. : Fe = 26]
questions.solution:
(a) Energies of $d_{x^2-y^2}$ and $d_{z^2}$ ($e_g$ orbitals) are raised because their lobes lie directly along the coordinate axes where incoming ligands approach, causing greater electrostatic repulsion.
(b) $\text{Co}^{3+}$ has $d^6$ configuration.
(i) $\text{F}^-$ is a weak field ligand ($\Delta_o < P$): $t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$.
(ii) $\text{NH}_3$ is a strong field ligand ($\Delta_o > P$): $t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$.
(c) In $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$, $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ ($3d^8$) has $\text{Cl}^-$ as weak field ligand; no pairing occurs, leading to 2 unpaired electrons ($sp^3$, paramagnetic). In $[\text{Ni(CO)}_4]$, CO is a strong field ligand that forces pairing of electrons to give $3d^{10}$ configuration ($sp^3$, diamagnetic).
OR
(c) In $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{3-}$, $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ($3d^5$) pairs up due to strong field $\text{CN}^-$ ligand leaving 1 unpaired electron. Hybridization: $d^2sp^3$, Magnetic behaviour: Paramagnetic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
(a) (i) An organic compound (X) has the molecular formula $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$. Draw structures for (X) if it :
(I) does not give Tollen's test but gives a positive iodoform test.
(II) does not give Tollen's test and iodoform test but undergoes Aldol condensation.
(III) undergoes Cannizzaro's reaction.
(ii) Show how each of the following compounds can be converted to benzoic acid :
(I) Acetophenone
(II) Ethyl benzene

OR

(b) Answer the following questions :
(i) Draw structure of the 2, 4-dinitrophenyl hydrazone derivative of benzaldehyde.
(ii) Arrange the following in increasing order of their reactivity towards HCN :
Di-tert. butyl ketone, Acetaldehyde, Acetone
(iii) Give a simple chemical test to distinguish between benzoic acid and ethyl benzoate.
(iv) Write the name of the reagent to convert Ethanenitrile to Ethanal.
(v) Draw the structure of 'X' in the reaction: Cyclohexanol $\xrightarrow{\text{CrO}_3}$ 'X'.
questions.solution:
(a) (i)
(I) Pentan-2-one: $\text{CH}_3\text{-CO-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH}_3$.
(II) Pentan-3-one: $\text{CH}_3\text{-CH}_2\text{-CO-CH}_2\text{-CH}_3$.
(III) 2,2-Dimethylpropanal: $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-CHO}$.
(ii) (I) Acetophenone $\xrightarrow{\text{NaOH + I}_2 / \text{NaOI}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COONa} + \text{CHI}_3 \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COOH}$.
(II) Ethylbenzene $\xrightarrow{\text{KMnO}_4 / \text{KOH, } \Delta} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COOK} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COOH}$.

OR

(b) (i) $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{-CH=N-NH-C}_6\text{H}_3(2,4-\text{NO}_2)_2$.
(ii) Di-tert. butyl ketone < Acetone < Acetaldehyde.
(iii) $\text{NaHCO}_3$ test: Benzoic acid gives brisk effervescence of $\text{CO}_2$ gas, whereas ethyl benzoate does not react.
(iv) DIBAL-H (Diisobutylaluminium hydride) followed by hydrolysis / $\text{SnCl}_2 + \text{HCl}$.
(v) 'X' is Cyclohexanone.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
(a) (i) From the given data of $E^\circ$ values, answer the following questions :

| $E^\circ_{M^{2+}/M}$ | V | Cr | Mn | Fe | Co | Ni | Cu |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Value (V) | -1.18 | -0.91 | -1.18 | -0.44 | -0.28 | -0.25 | +0.34 |

(I) Why $E^\circ_{M^{2+}/M}$ show irregular trend in the above values ?
(II) Why is $E^\circ_{\text{Cu}^{2+}/\text{Cu}}$ value exceptionally positive ?
(III) Why $E^\circ_{\text{Mn}^{2+}/\text{Mn}}$ value is highly negative ?
(ii) Write the ionic equations for the oxidising action of potassium permanganate for its reaction with $\text{I}^-$ in both acidic and alkaline solutions.

OR

(b) Answer the following questions :
(i) Name a member of the lanthanoid series (I) which exhibits +4 oxidation state, (II) which exhibits +2 oxidation state.
(ii) Why transition metals act as good catalyst ?
(iii) Why Cr has higher melting point than Mn ?
(iv) What happens when acidic solution of potassium permanganate is allowed to stand for sometime ? Give the equation involved. What is this type of reaction called ?
questions.solution:
(a) (i)
(I) Irregular trend is due to irregular variation in ionization enthalpies ($\Delta_i H_1 + \Delta_i H_2$) and enthalpy of sublimation.
(II) High enthalpy of atomization and high sum of ionization enthalpies of Cu are not balanced by its enthalpy of hydration.
(III) Due to stable half-filled $d^5$ electronic configuration of $\text{Mn}^{2+}$ ion.
(ii) Acidic medium: $2\text{MnO}_4^- + 10\text{I}^- + 16\text{H}^+ \longrightarrow 2\text{Mn}^{2+} + 5\text{I}_2 + 8\text{H}_2\text{O}$
Alkaline medium: $2\text{MnO}_4^- + \text{I}^- + \text{H}_2\text{O} \longrightarrow 2\text{MnO}_2 + \text{IO}_3^- + 2\text{OH}^-$

OR

(b) (i) (I) Cerium (Ce), (II) Europium (Eu).
(ii) They show variable oxidation states and provide large surface area for adsorption.
(iii) Chromium has 6 unpaired electrons per atom ($3d^5 4s^1$), leading to strong metallic bonding, while Mn has stable $3d^5 4s^2$ with tightly bound $4s$ electrons resulting in weaker metallic bonding.
(iv) Acidic $\text{KMnO}_4$ slowly decomposes liberating oxygen gas:
$4\text{MnO}_4^- + 12\text{H}^+ \longrightarrow 4\text{Mn}^{2+} + 5\text{O}_2 + 6\text{H}_2\text{O}$. This is an auto-decomposition / redox reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
(a) Calculate emf and $\Delta G$ for the following cell at $298\text{ K}$ :
$$\text{Mg}(s) \mid \text{Mg}^{2+}(0.01\text{ M}) \parallel \text{Ag}^+(0.001\text{ M}) \mid \text{Ag}(s)$$
Given : $E^\circ_{\text{Mg}^{2+}/\text{Mg}} = -2.37\text{ V}$, $E^\circ_{\text{Ag}^+/\text{Ag}} = +0.80\text{ V}$
[$1\text{ F} = 96500\text{ C mol}^{-1}, \log 10 = 1$]

OR

(b) For the reaction :
$$2\text{AgCl}(s) + \text{H}_2(g)(0.4\text{ atm}) \longrightarrow 2\text{Ag}(s) + 2\text{H}^+(0.1\text{ M}) + 2\text{Cl}^-(0.2\text{ M})$$
Calculate emf of the cell at $25^\circ\text{C}$.
Given : $\Delta G^\circ = -43500\text{ J mol}^{-1}$, $[\log 10 = 1, 1\text{ F} = 96500\text{ C mol}^{-1}]$
questions.solution:
(a)
1. $E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = E^\circ_{\text{cathode}} - E^\circ_{\text{anode}} = 0.80 - (-2.37) = 3.17\text{ V}$.
2. Cell reaction: $\text{Mg}(s) + 2\text{Ag}^+(aq) \longrightarrow \text{Mg}^{2+}(aq) + 2\text{Ag}(s)$, $n = 2$.
3. Nernst equation: $E_{\text{cell}} = E^\circ_{\text{cell}} - \frac{0.0591}{2} \log \frac{[\text{Mg}^{2+}]}{[\text{Ag}^+]^2} = 3.17 - 0.02955 \log \frac{10^{-2}}{(10^{-3})^2} = 3.17 - 0.02955 \log (10^4) = 3.17 - 0.1182 = 3.0518\text{ V}$.
4. $\Delta G = -nFE_{\text{cell}} = -2 \times 96500 \times 3.0518 = -589000\text{ J mol}^{-1} = -589\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

OR

(b)
1. $E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = -\frac{\Delta G^\circ}{nF} = -\frac{-43500}{2 \times 96500} = 0.225\text{ V}$.
2. Reaction quotient $Q = \frac{[\text{H}^+]^2 [\text{Cl}^-]^2}{P_{\text{H}_2}} = \frac{(0.1)^2 (0.2)^2}{0.4} = \frac{10^{-2} \times 4 \times 10^{-2}}{0.4} = 10^{-3}$.
3. $E_{\text{cell}} = E^\circ_{\text{cell}} - \frac{0.0591}{2} \log 10^{-3} = 0.225 - 0.02955 (-3) = 0.225 + 0.08865 = 0.31365\text{ V} \approx 0.314\text{ V}$.
